parsed_response.reasoning: In the new parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts, the schema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, both of which evaluate to the literal '[object Object]' (zod schemas stringify to '[object Object]'), so the second overwrites the first. The resulting object schema only declares `access_token` plus a '[object Object]' key, and strips all other properties (zod default behavior). When credential sharing is enabled, Salesforce's response loses instance_url/signature before being persisted via prisma.credential.update, and O365's parsed token data would have its real refresh_token replaced by the literal sentinel string 'refresh_token' (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token" }`), breaking subsequent local refresh. This is verifiable directly from the diff's new code.

judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys both evaluate to the literal '[object Object]' (zod schemas don't stringify into key names), so the second key overwrites the first and the schema strips everything except access_token — Salesforce loses instance_url so jsforce connections fail from the second use onward, and O365 has its real refresh_token overwritten with the sentinel literal 'refresh_token' and no expiry, making local refresh impossible if sharing is later disabled
